status_label: Truce Extended to Jan 10, 2027 — China's 10% Still On; US Import Bans on Some Canadian Goods Sep 29
status_note:
WHAT APPLIES TODAY. US soybeans into China face roughly 13% (3% MFN + China's broad 10% retaliatory levy); corn and wheat about 11%, pork about 22%. The July 6 report that China would drop the 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1 has NOT been borne out: on Sep 24, 2026, with the Trump-Xi meeting under way, the rate on US soybeans was still described as 13%. Treat it as unresolved rather than imminent.

THE TRUCE RUNS LONGER. On Sep 24, 2026 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Busan agreement, due to end Nov 10, would be extended to Jan 10, 2027 — "to give us more time to see what we can do on the economic front." Trump and Xi met Sep 24-25. China's purchase commitment is 25 MMT of soybeans a year for 2026-2028, and it was roughly halfway through the 2026 figure by Sep 17 after buying about 1 MMT in a week. A further roughly $17B a year of other US farm purchases remains behind pace.

TARIFF AUTHORITY. SCOTUS voided the IEEPA tariffs on Feb 20, 2026. The Section 122 surcharge that replaced them was ruled invalid by the Court of International Trade on May 7, 2026 (under appeal) and lapsed around Jul 24. Section 301 'forced labor' duties took effect Jul 24, 2026 at 10-12.5% across 60 trading partners and about 99.4% of US imports. Farm inputs are explicitly exempt: in-quota sugar, fertilizer and pesticides, and certain planting seeds.

NORTH AMERICA, AND THIS IS THE LIVE ONE. Canada's counter-tariffs took effect Sep 8, 2026 — C$27.6B of US imports at 15%, 25% and 50%, covering steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics. Dairy runs 25-50%; honey and molasses are at 50%. Bulk grain, oilseeds, soybeans, corn, wheat, fertilizer and seeds are NOT on the list, so the 0% rows above are unchanged. The same day the President signed five Section 338 proclamations responding to it: import BANS on certain Canadian alcohol and dairy effective Sep 29, 2026, and list changes effective Sep 15 that removed rock salt and cement and added all-terrain vehicles and further dairy. This is an escalation cycle running through a USMCA renegotiation, and August's 50% Section 338 duties already overrode USMCA origin once.

BRAZIL. A 25% tariff on Brazilian goods including ethanol landed mid-July after a Section 301 investigation — an inbound tariff that structurally favours US corn ethanol at home.

Verify against USTR, the Federal Register and Canada's Department of Finance before any trading decision.
headline: The Oct 1 removal of China's 10% levy did NOT happen: US soybeans still face about 13% as of Sep 24, and Treasury has extended the Busan truce from Nov 10, 2026 to Jan 10, 2027. China is roughly halfway through its 25 MMT soybean commitment. Canada's C$27.6B counter-tariffs took effect Sep 8 and do not touch bulk grain, oilseeds, fertilizer or seeds; US import bans on certain Canadian alcohol and dairy follow on Sep 29.

rows.note: China lifted its March 2025 retaliatory 10% on soybeans under the Busan agreement (effective Nov 10, 2025) but kept its broad 10% 'Liberation Day' retaliatory levy — so US soybeans face roughly 13% (3% MFN + 10%), a persistent disadvantage vs. Brazil. A Section 301 investigation is pending and could re-escalate. Watch: the reported Jul 6 deal would have dropped this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1. It has not happened — the rate was still being quoted at its current level on Sep 24, 2026, and the Busan truce now runs to Jan 10, 2027.

China suspended its March 2025 retaliatory 15% on corn under the Busan agreement but kept the broad 10% retaliatory levy, leaving roughly 11% (1% MFN + 10%). China purchases remain below pre-trade-war levels; Brazil retains market share. Watch: the reported Jul 6 deal would have dropped this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1. It has not happened — the rate was still being quoted at its current level on Sep 24, 2026, and the Busan truce now runs to Jan 10, 2027.

March 2025 retaliatory 15% suspended under the Busan agreement; the broad 10% retaliatory levy remains (~11% = 1% MFN + 10%). US wheat has modest direct China exposure — global trade flows matter more than this rate. Watch: the reported Jul 6 deal would have dropped this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1. It has not happened — the rate was still being quoted at its current level on Sep 24, 2026, and the Busan truce now runs to Jan 10, 2027.

March 2025 retaliatory 10% suspended under the Busan agreement; the broad 10% retaliatory levy remains (~22% = 12% MFN + 10%). China resumed US beef and poultry access under the May 18, 2026 deal and remains a major US pork market. Watch: the reported Jul 6 deal would have dropped this 10% for cargoes arriving after Oct 1. It has not happened — the rate was still being quoted at its current level on Sep 24, 2026, and the Busan truce now runs to Jan 10, 2027.

USMCA-compliant, duty-free. USMCA joint review underway (US-Mexico bilateral rounds began May 2026). Penn Wharton: USMCA exemption share reached 86.3% of Canada/Mexico imports by February 2026. USMCA renegotiation opened July 2026 — rates unchanged so far, but the framework itself is now in play. Aug 2026: 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian dairy, alcohol and vehicles applied DESPITE USMCA origin. Canada's C$27.6B counter-tariffs then took effect Sep 8 at 15-50% on steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics — bulk grain, oilseeds, fertilizer and seeds are NOT on the list, confirmed against Canada's own published schedule, so this rate is unchanged. US import bans on certain Canadian alcohol and dairy follow Sep 29.

USMCA-compliant, duty-free. Mexico remains the top US corn export destination; Canadian demand steady. USMCA joint review underway. USMCA renegotiation opened July 2026 — rates unchanged so far, but the framework itself is now in play. Aug 2026: 50% Section 338 duties on Canadian dairy, alcohol and vehicles applied DESPITE USMCA origin. Canada's C$27.6B counter-tariffs then took effect Sep 8 at 15-50% on steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics — bulk grain, oilseeds, fertilizer and seeds are NOT on the list, confirmed against Canada's own published schedule, so this rate is unchanged. US import bans on certain Canadian alcohol and dairy follow Sep 29.

No EU anti-dumping duty on US ethanol. The 2013 duty was repealed by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/765, in force 16 May 2019, and the proceeding was terminated. What remains is the ordinary Common Customs Tariff import duty — €192/m³ undenatured, €102/m³ denatured — which applies EU-wide, not by member state. The Dutch RED III vote of Oct 2025 bars imported denatured ethanol from counting toward renewable-fuel obligations from 2026; that is a compliance rule, not a duty. The UK-US deal (May 2025) opened a 1.4B L/yr duty-free quota for the UK only. Verify member-state customs for specific shipments.

timeline.event: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the Busan truce, due to end Nov 10, will be extended to Jan 10, 2027. US soybeans into China are still quoted at 13% (10% reciprocal + 3% MFN) as Trump and Xi meet Sep 24-25 — the reported Oct 1 removal of the 10% has not taken effect.
China is roughly halfway through its 25 MMT 2026 soybean commitment after buying about 1 MMT in a week. The 10% levy still makes US beans less attractive to private Chinese crushers.

The President signs five Section 338 proclamations in response to Canada: import bans on certain Canadian alcohol and dairy effective Sep 29, 2026, plus list changes effective Sep 15 removing rock salt and cement and adding all-terrain vehicles and further dairy products.

Canada's counter-tariffs take effect: C$27.6B of US imports at 15%, 25% and 50% across steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics. Bulk grain, oilseeds, fertilizer and seeds are not on the published list.
Canada retaliates with $27.6B in counter-tariffs: 50% on certain steel and aluminum, 25% on fish and tools. No bulk agricultural commodity is named in the Canadian list.

US imposes 50% Section 338 duties on roughly $20B of Canadian imports — dairy (notably TRQ cheese), alcoholic beverages and motor vehicles, plus a longer covered list that reaches honey, certain planting seeds, molasses and fructose syrups. Grain and oilseeds are NOT covered. The date differs by source: counsel reported it effective Aug 19, customs brokers put it at 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 22 for entries on or after that date — confirm the entry date for a specific shipment. Critically, USMCA origin does NOT exempt covered goods, which is the first time duty-free USMCA treatment has been overridden outright while the agreement is being renegotiated.

China is roughly a quarter of the way through its 25 MMT/yr soybean commitment for 2026 — behind pace with a Trump-Xi meeting expected in September. Buying accelerated into that meeting; private crushers reportedly held back.

Section 301 'forced labor' duties take effect at 10-12.5% across 60 trading partners, covering about 99.4% of US imports and replacing the lapsed Section 122 surcharge (goods in transit had a grace period to July 28). Agricultural exemptions apply universally to in-quota sugar, FERTILIZER AND PESTICIDES, and certain planting seeds — input costs are shielded. Five economies were cut to 10% after forced-labour import bans or trade commitments; the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan get a modified MFN-ceiling method where existing duties count toward the cap instead of stacking on top.

USMCA bilateral negotiations resume in Mexico City — the first talks since the Administration signaled it would not renew the agreement. No ag rate changes announced; Canada/Mexico access (top two US ag export destinations) rides on the outcome.

25% tariff on Brazilian goods, including ethanol, announced the prior week following a Section 301 investigation. Inbound tariff: Brazilian ethanol had been gaining US market share — this structurally improves US corn ethanol's domestic position.

Reported deal to unwind the last ag levy: the US would end its 10% fentanyl tariff and China would reciprocate by dropping its 10% tax on US agricultural goods, targeted at cargoes ARRIVING AFTER OCTOBER 1 — timed to when China normally shifts from Brazilian to US supply. China's Ministry of Commerce confirmed the agreement; USTR had not confirmed it at the time of reporting. This is the levy that keeps US soybeans near 13%, so it is the single line item on this page most worth watching.

The Administration signals it will not renew USMCA and will instead open new negotiations. House Ag Democrats and ag groups flag the risk: tariff-free access hits corn, beef, pork, and dairy before anything else.

USTR proposes Section 301 'forced labor' tariffs of 10-12.5% on 59 countries and the EU, with some agricultural exemptions (Annex A). Public comment runs to July 6, hearing July 7 — timed to maintain duties after the Section 122 surcharge expires around July 24.

US-China deal during President Trump's state visit: China to buy at least $17B/yr in US agricultural products through 2028 (in addition to the Oct 2025 soybean commitments) and resumes purchases of US beef and poultry.

US Court of International Trade rules the Section 122 global 10% surcharge (Proclamation 11012) invalid for failing to identify the required balance-of-payments deficit (Oregon v. United States; Burlap & Barrel v. United States). The ruling is under appeal and does not automatically halt collections.

Section 122 global tariff takes effect at 10% (administration announced intent to raise to 15%) after the IEEPA tariffs were terminated. The 150-day statutory clock runs to roughly July 24, 2026 unless Congress extends it.

US Supreme Court rules 6-3 in Learning Resources v. Trump that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; the April 2025 reciprocal and fentanyl tariffs are voided. The administration pivots to Section 122 the same day.
China lifts the up-to-15% retaliatory ag tariffs from its March 2025 tranche under the Busan agreement, but keeps the broad 10% 'Liberation Day' retaliatory levy — leaving US soybeans at roughly 13%.

Trump-Xi meeting in Busan, South Korea: tariff truce reached. China commits to buy 12 MMT of US soybeans in late 2025 and 25 MMT/yr in 2026-2028; the truce is later extended through Nov 10, 2026, and again to Jan 10, 2027.
China imposes first-tranche retaliatory tariffs on US ag (15% on wheat, corn, cotton, chicken; 10% on soybeans, pork, beef, dairy) — later suspended under the Oct 30, 2025 Busan agreement.
